notice: Short original paraphrases for simulator coaching. These are mechanisms and testable hypotheses, not diagnoses made without telemetry.

sources.title: The Six Phases of a Corner
Understanding the Importance of Car Setup for Beginners
The Ultimate Guide to Braking on Track

principles.title: Compare the same place on track
principles.mechanism: Align speed, brake and throttle against distance. A lap-time difference alone cannot identify the driver's input that caused it.
principles.check: Compare braking onset, minimum speed and throttle pickup with a clean, compatible reference.
principles.experiment: Change one input in one corner, then inspect the resulting section time.
principles.limitations: Traffic, grip, fuel and setup differences can confound the comparison.

principles.title: Brake release affects entry balance
principles.mechanism: Reducing brake load as steering rises changes how the car shares grip between slowing and turning.
principles.check: Inspect the shape and repeatability of brake release alongside steering and entry speed.
principles.experiment: Keep the braking landmark fixed and try a smoother release; judge the exit as well as entry.
principles.limitations: The appropriate overlap depends on corner speed, car balance and available grip. More trail braking is not always faster.

principles.title: A faster entry can spoil the exit
principles.mechanism: Arriving beyond the corner's useful entry speed can delay rotation and throttle application.
principles.check: Compare the complete corner and following acceleration zone, not only the braking point.
principles.experiment: Test a slightly more controlled entry and keep it only if the measured section improves.
principles.limitations: This is a hypothesis to test, not proof that a lower entry speed is the solution.

principles.title: Abrupt inputs can upset an already loaded car
principles.mechanism: A sudden steering or brake-release change can demand grip faster than the tyres and chassis can accommodate.
principles.check: Look for repeated input steps and lost speed at the same position across several clean laps.
principles.experiment: Use a more progressive transition while keeping the rest of the corner unchanged.
principles.limitations: Input variation alone does not establish understeer, oversteer or a suspension fault.

principles.title: Build throttle as the steering unwinds
principles.mechanism: As turning demand falls on exit, more of the tyre's capacity can be used for acceleration.
principles.check: Compare sustained throttle pickup, steering reduction and exit speed with a compatible clean lap.
principles.experiment: Aim for a repeatable progressive pickup; retain the change only if the following straight is faster.
principles.limitations: Early throttle can be counterproductive when the car still needs to rotate or traction is limited.

principles.title: Explain the pedal transition before calling it a mistake
principles.mechanism: Time without brake or throttle can reveal a delayed transition, but a corner also has a deliberate balancing phase.
principles.check: Locate extra neutral-pedal time against a faster comparable lap and check whether speed or exit actually suffered.
principles.experiment: Work on one transition at a time rather than trying to eliminate every lift.
principles.limitations: Fuel saving, traffic, low grip and car rotation can justify a lift; zero coasting is not a universal target.

principles.title: Pedal percentage is not a universal braking target
principles.mechanism: Useful braking depends on tyre grip, speed, load and assistance systems; maximum pedal input can lock a non-ABS car.
principles.check: Relate the brake trace to deceleration and corner outcome for this car.
principles.experiment: Use a consistent landmark and compare the braking profile, rather than chasing a fixed percentage.
principles.limitations: A pedal trace alone does not prove brake pressure, tyre lock or ABS intervention.

principles.title: Identify the corner phase before a setup experiment
principles.mechanism: The same balance complaint can arise for different reasons on entry, at the apex or under power.
principles.check: Combine the driver's report with repeated data from that phase before selecting a change.
principles.experiment: Save a baseline, change one setting and compare several repeatable laps under similar conditions.
principles.limitations: Generic setup advice is not an exact spring, pressure or differential prescription for an unknown AC mod.
